data:
Status: released v0.1.0.
Sparse matrices, fill-reducing orderings and iterative solvers in pure Go (CGO_ENABLED=0), module github.com/go-sparse/sparse, BSD-3-Clause.
go get github.com/go-sparse/sparse@v0.1.0 a := gallery.Laplacian2D(100, 100) // *sparse.CSR[float64] b := make([]float64, a.Rows) ic, _ := iter.NewIC0(a) // incomplete Cholesky res, _ := iter.CG(a, b, &iter.Options{RTol: 1e-8, M: ic}) fmt.Println(res.Info, res.Iterations) // 0 = converged, as in SciPy
data.orderings-provenance#Orderings: provenan: AMD and COLAMD are written from the papers (Amestoy, Davis and Duff, 1996; Davis, Gilbert, Larimore and Ng, 2004). SuiteSparse AMD and COLAMD are the reference algorithms; CHOLMOD, UMFPACK and CSparse (GPL/LGPL) were not consulted. Tie-breaking differs, so permutations differ; quality is compared by fill.
data.performance#Performance:
One core, Go 1.27.2 on darwin/arm64, SciPy 1.18.1, medians of 7 interleaved rounds. Ratio is Go time / SciPy time; below 1 means Go is faster. From the library’s docs/perf.md, measured on 2026-10-20 at load 5.
work SpMV CG GMRES(30) 2-D Laplacian, 1.1e5 nonzeros 0.97 0.70 0.56 2-D Laplacian, 1.0e6 nonzeros 0.98 0.89 0.82 Column indices are int32, as in scipy.sparse; dot products and vector updates use the fleet’s SIMD kernels, and the Krylov solvers fuse each vector update with the dot product that follows it.
data.quality-gates#Quality gates: gofmt, go vet, go test -race with 100% statement coverage over all packages, 386 and the other architectures in CI, and govulncheck.
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: mtx.ReadLimited takes limits on dimensions, entries, line length, decompressed size and comment lines; declared sizes are checked before allocation, and a gzip bomb is cut off at the byte limit. mtx.FuzzRead has a committed corpus.
data.verification#Verification:
Every solver, LSQR and LSMR and the orderings are compared with SciPy 1.18.1 and NumPy 2.5.4 (and SuiteSparse AMD through cvxopt as a binary oracle). A Go harness drives SciPy over a pipe and records the answers in a committed fixture; the regression tests replay it, so they need neither Python nor network. The full method is the library’s docs/verification.md.
On the committed suite: CG, GMRES, MINRES, LSQR and LSMR iteration counts equal SciPy’s; BiCGSTAB agrees within a few iterations. AMD Cholesky fill is within 1% of SuiteSparse AMD; COLAMD LU fill is within 4% of SuperLU’s COLAMD; RCM bandwidth equals SciPy’s.
data.what-is-provided#What is provided:
package provides sparse COO, CSR, CSC, DOK over float64 and complex128; conversions; O(1) transpose; SpMV, SpMM, SpGEMM; Add, Sub, Axpby; scaling; Diagonal, Tril, Triu, Permute, Prune, norms; Eye, Diags; LinearOperator nd *ndarray.Array in and out: vectors, dense matrices, SpMV and SpMM mtx Matrix Market read and write: coordinate and array, real, integer, pattern and complex, general, symmetric, skew-symmetric and hermitian, gzip input order RCM, AMD, COLAMD; Bandwidth, Profile, CholeskyNNZ, QRFillNNZ iter CG, GMRES(m), BiCGSTAB, MINRES, LSQR, LSMR; preconditioners Jacobi, SSOR, IC0, ILU0, ILUT gallery Laplacians (1-D, 2-D, 3-D), convection-diffusion, seeded random sparse matrices Solvers follow scipy.sparse.linalg: the stopping rule is ‖b − A x‖ ≤ max(rtol·‖b‖, atol), rtol defaults to 1e-5, maxiter to 10n (5n for MINRES), and info is 0 on success, the iteration limit when it was reached, and negative on breakdown.
Not provided yet: sparse direct factorisations (LU, Cholesky, QR), nested dissection, eigensolvers, algebraic multigrid, Rutherford-Boeing I/O.
